mn11:0.2: The Shorter Discourse on the Lion’s Roar
mn11:1.2: On one occasion the Blessed One was living at Sāvatthī in Jeta’s Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika’s Park.
mn11:1.3: There he addressed the bhikkhus thus:
mn11:2.1: “Bhikkhus, only here is there a recluse, only here a second recluse, only here a third recluse, only here a fourth recluse.
mn11:2.2: The doctrines of others are devoid of recluses:
mn11:2.3: that is how you should rightly roar your lion’s roar.
mn11:3.1: “It is possible, bhikkhus, that wanderers of other sects might ask:
mn11:3.2: ‘But on the strength of what argument or with the support of what authority do the venerable ones say thus?’
mn11:3.5: Wanderers of other sects who ask thus may be answered in this way:
mn11:3.6: ‘Friends, four things have been declared to us by the Blessed One who knows and sees, accomplished and fully enlightened; on seeing these in ourselves we say thus:
mn11:3.7: “Only here is there a recluse, only here a second recluse, only here a third recluse, only here a fourth recluse.
mn11:3.8: The doctrines of others are devoid of recluses.”
mn11:3.10: We have confidence in the Teacher, we have confidence in the Dhamma, we have fulfilled the precepts,
mn11:3.11: and our companions in the Dhamma are dear and agreeable to us
mn11:3.12: whether they are laymen or those gone forth.
mn11:3.13: These are the four things declared to us by the Blessed One who knows and sees, accomplished and fully enlightened, on seeing which in ourselves we say as we do.’
mn11:4.1: “It is possible, bhikkhus, that wanderers of other sects might say thus:
mn11:4.2: ‘Friends, we too have confidence in the Teacher, that is, in our Teacher; we too have confidence in the Dhamma, that is, in our Dhamma; we too have fulfilled the precepts, that is, our precepts;
mn11:4.3: and our companions in the Dhamma are dear and agreeable to us too
mn11:4.4: whether they are laymen or those gone forth.
mn11:4.5: What is the distinction here, friends, what is the variance, what is the difference between you and us?’
mn11:5.1: “Wanderers of other sects who ask thus may be answered in this way:
mn11:5.2: ‘How then, friends, is the goal one or many?’
mn11:5.3: Answering rightly, the wanderers of other sects would answer thus:
mn11:5.4: ‘Friends, the goal is one, not many.’—
mn11:5.5: ‘But, friends, is that goal for one affected by lust or free from lust?’
mn11:5.6: Answering rightly, the wanderers of other sects would answer thus:
mn11:5.7: ‘Friends, that goal is for one free from lust, not for one affected by lust.’—
mn11:5.8: ‘But, friends, is that goal for one affected by hate or free from hate?’
mn11:5.10: ‘Friends, that goal is for one free from hate, not for one affected by hate.’—
mn11:5.11: ‘But, friends, is that goal for one affected by delusion or free from delusion?’
mn11:5.13: ‘Friends, that goal is for one free from delusion, not for one affected by delusion.’—
mn11:5.14: ‘But, friends, is that goal for one affected by craving or free from craving? ’
mn11:5.16: ‘Friends, that goal is for one free from craving, not for one affected by craving. ’—
mn11:5.17: ‘But, friends, is that goal for one affected by clinging or free from clinging?’
mn11:5.19: ‘Friends, that goal is for one free from clinging, not for one affected by clinging.’—
mn11:5.20: ‘But, friends, is that goal for one who has vision or for one without vision?’
mn11:5.22: ‘Friends, that goal is for one with vision, not for one without vision.’—
mn11:5.23: ‘But, friends, is that goal for one who favours and opposes, or for one who does not favour and oppose?’
mn11:5.25: ‘Friends, that goal is for one who does not favour and oppose, not for one who favours and opposes.’—
mn11:5.26: ‘But, friends, is that goal for one who delights in and enjoys proliferation, or for one who does not delight in and enjoy proliferation?’
mn11:5.28: ‘Friends, that goal is for one who does not delight in and enjoy proliferation, not for one who delights in and enjoys proliferation.’
mn11:6.2: the view of being and the view of non-being.
mn11:6.3: Any recluses or brahmins who rely on the view of being, adopt the view of being, accept the view of being, are opposed to the view of non-being.
mn11:6.4: Any recluses or brahmins who rely on the view of non-being, adopt the view of non-being, accept the view of non-being, are opposed to the view of being.
mn11:7.1: “Any recluses or brahmins who do not understand as they actually are the origin, the disappearance, the gratification, the danger, and the escape in the case of these two views are affected by lust, affected by hate, affected by delusion, affected by craving, affected by clinging, without vision, given to favouring and opposing, and they delight in and enjoy proliferation.
mn11:7.2: They are not freed from birth, ageing, and death; from sorrow, lamentation, pain, grief, and despair;
mn11:7.3: they are not freed from suffering, I say.
mn11:8.1: “Any recluses or brahmins who understand as they actually are the origin, the disappearance, the gratification, the danger, and the escape in the case of these two views are without lust, without hate, without delusion, without craving, without clinging, with vision, not given to favouring and opposing, and they do not delight in and enjoy proliferation.
mn11:8.2: They are freed from birth, ageing, and death; from sorrow, lamentation, pain, grief, and despair;
mn11:8.3: they are freed from suffering, I say.
mn11:9.1: “Bhikkhus, there are these four kinds of clinging.
mn11:9.3: Clinging to sensual pleasures, clinging to views, clinging to rules and observances, and clinging to a doctrine of self.
mn11:10.1: “Though certain recluses and brahmins claim to propound the full understanding of all kinds of clinging,
mn11:10.2: they do not completely describe the full understanding of all kinds of clinging.
mn11:10.3: They describe the full understanding of clinging to sensual pleasures without describing the full understanding of clinging to views, clinging to rules and observances, and clinging to a doctrine of self.
mn11:10.5: Those good recluses and brahmins do not understand these three instances of clinging as they actually are.
mn11:10.6: Therefore, though they claim to propound the full understanding of all kinds of clinging,
mn11:10.7: they describe only the full understanding of clinging to sensual pleasures without describing the full understanding of clinging to views, clinging to rules and observances, and clinging to a doctrine of self.
mn11:11.1: “Though certain recluses and brahmins claim to propound the full understanding of all kinds of clinging…they describe the full understanding of clinging to sensual pleasures and clinging to views without describing the full understanding of clinging to rules and observances and clinging to a doctrine of self.
mn11:11.5: They do not understand two instances…therefore they describe only the full understanding of clinging to sensual pleasures and clinging to views without describing the full understanding of clinging to rules and observances and clinging to a doctrine of self.
mn11:12.1: “Though certain recluses and brahmins claim to propound the full understanding of all kinds of clinging…they describe the full understanding of clinging to sensual pleasures,
mn11:12.3: clinging to views, and clinging to rules and observances without describing the full understanding of clinging to a doctrine of self.
mn11:12.5: They do not understand one instance…therefore they describe only the full understanding of clinging to sensual pleasures, clinging to views, and clinging to rules and observances without describing the full understanding of clinging to a doctrine of self.
mn11:13.1: “Bhikkhus, in such a Dhamma and Discipline as that, it is plain that confidence in the Teacher is not rightly directed,
mn11:13.2: that confidence in the Dhamma is not rightly directed,
mn11:13.3: that fulfilment of the precepts is not rightly directed,
mn11:13.4: and that the affection among companions in the Dhamma is not rightly directed.
mn11:13.6: Because that is how it is when the Dhamma and Discipline is badly proclaimed and badly expounded, unemancipating, unconducive to peace, expounded by one who is not fully enlightened.
mn11:14.1: “Bhikkhus, when a Tathāgata, accomplished and fully enlightened, claims to propound the full understanding of all kinds of clinging,
mn11:14.2: he completely describes the full understanding of all kinds of clinging: he describes the full understanding of clinging to sensual pleasures, clinging to views, clinging to rules and observances, and clinging to a doctrine of self.
mn11:15.1: “Bhikkhus, in such a Dhamma and Discipline as that, it is plain that confidence in the Teacher is rightly directed,
mn11:15.2: that confidence in the Dhamma is rightly directed,
mn11:15.3: that fulfilment of the precepts is rightly directed,
mn11:15.4: and that the affection among companions in the Dhamma is rightly directed.
mn11:15.6: Because that is how it is when the Dhamma and Discipline is well proclaimed and well expounded, emancipating, conducive to peace, expounded by one who is fully enlightened.
mn11:16.1: “Now these four kinds of clinging have what as their source, what as their origin, from what are they born and produced?
mn11:16.2: These four kinds of clinging have craving as their source, craving as their origin, they are born and produced from craving.
mn11:16.3: Craving has what as its source…?
mn11:16.4: Craving has feeling as its source…Feeling has what as its source…?
mn11:16.6: Feeling has contact as its source…Contact has what as its source…?
mn11:16.8: Contact has the sixfold base as its source…The sixfold base has what as its source…?
mn11:16.10: The sixfold base has mentality-materiality as its source…Mentality-materiality has what as its source…?
mn11:16.12: Mentality-materiality has consciousness as its source…Consciousness has what as its source…?
mn11:16.14: Consciousness has formations as its source…Formations have what as their source…?
mn11:16.16: Formations have ignorance as their source, ignorance as their origin, they are born and produced from ignorance.
mn11:17.1: “Bhikkhus, when ignorance is abandoned and true knowledge has arisen in a bhikkhu, then with the fading away of ignorance and the arising of true knowledge he no longer clings to sensual pleasures, no longer clings to views, no longer clings to rules and observances, no longer clings to a doctrine of self.
mn11:17.2: When he does not cling, he is not agitated. When he is not agitated, he personally attains Nibbāna.
mn11:17.3: He understands: ‘Birth is destroyed, the holy life has been lived, what had to be done has been done, there is no more coming to any state of being.’”
mn11:17.4: That is what the Blessed One said.
mn11:17.5: The bhikkhus were satisfied and delighted in the Blessed One’s words.
